- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows sharp downward trend after a recent high, check for lag: true price often rebounds within 3–5 days; adjust forecast to include early mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.2) and model forecasts continue downward, consider mean reversion bias — add 2–5% upward correction if price hasn’t fallen below 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently underestimates prices after a 10–15% drop in recent history, apply a “recovery bias” — add 3–7% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.6), model often misreads momentum — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal lag: delay peak or trough by 1–2 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and model shows high volatility, reduce forecast variance — assume 70% of price movement is noise; use 30-day moving average as anchor.
